questions.prompt: Which React hook is specifically designed for handling lifecycle side-effects such as subscriptions and manual DOM mutations?
questions.explanation: useEffect runs after render and is the designated hook for synchronization and side effects in React function components.

questions.prompt: Why should you pass a function to the state setter `setCount(prev => prev + 1)` instead of `setCount(count + 1)` inside asynchronous callbacks?
options: It guarantees access to the latest state value even during batched or concurrent updates
It forces synchronous execution of the state update
It automatically memoizes the callback result
questions.explanation: Functional state updates avoid stale closures by receiving the most recent queued state from React.

questions.prompt: When optimizing a component with `React.memo`, when will it re-render even if its primitive props have not changed?
options: When an inline object/callback prop is created anew each render and fails reference equality (===)
Only when the browser window is resized
Only when the Redux store is completely cleared
questions.explanation: React.memo performs shallow comparison (`Object.is`) on props. Un-memoized object references break shallow equality.

questions.prompt: What is the primary difference between `unknown` and `any` in TypeScript?
options: unknown requires type narrowing or type assertions before operations can be performed on it; any disables type checking
any is type-safe whereas unknown allows any runtime operation without checks
unknown can only store primitive string values
There is no difference; they are direct aliases
questions.explanation: unknown is the type-safe counterpart of any, requiring type guards before accessing properties.

questions.prompt: Which TypeScript utility type constructs a type with all properties of T set to optional?
questions.explanation: Partial<T> marks all properties of type T as optional.

questions.prompt: What does the `infer` keyword do inside conditional types in TypeScript?
options: Deduces a type variable within the `extends` clause for extraction
Forces TypeScript to infer all functions as asynchronous
Suppresses compiler errors for missing exports
questions.explanation: The infer keyword introduces a type variable to be deduced from another type structure inside conditional types.

questions.prompt: In the Node.js event loop, which phase executes callbacks scheduled by `process.nextTick()`?
options: The microtask queue immediately after the current operation finishes, before the next event loop phase
The Close callbacks phase at the very end of process exit
The Poll phase during I/O polling
questions.explanation: nextTickQueue is resolved immediately after the current operation finishes, preceding the next event loop phase and Promise microtasks.

questions.prompt: What happens if a Node.js stream is not paused or piped and data is emitted faster than the consumer can process it?
options: Memory consumption grows unbounded (lack of backpressure)
Node automatically spawns worker threads to handle overflow
The stream silently drops all excess packets without error
The operating system restarts the Node.js process
questions.explanation: Without backpressure handling or proper piping, unconsumed data buffers in memory, leading to memory leaks or process crashes.

questions.prompt: Which Node.js core module should be used to run CPU-intensive tasks without blocking the main event loop?
questions.explanation: worker_threads enables running JavaScript in parallel on separate threads with shared memory or message passing.

questions.prompt: What parameters must an Express error-handling middleware function declare?
questions.explanation: Express identifies error-handling middleware by checking function.length === 4 (err, req, res, next).

questions.prompt: In Express 5, how are rejected promises returned from route handlers handled?
options: Express 5 automatically catches rejected promises and routes them to next(err)
They crash the server unless wrapped in try/catch or async-error-handler
They are ignored and client receives HTTP 200 with empty body
questions.explanation: Express 5 natively forwards rejected promises returned from route handlers to the error-handling middleware.

questions.prompt: Which HTTP method should be used for idempotent full replacements of a resource?
questions.explanation: PUT is designated for idempotent updates replacing the entire resource representation.

questions.prompt: What HTTP status code should be returned when a resource creation succeeds asynchronously and is queued for processing?
questions.explanation: HTTP 202 Accepted indicates that the request has been received and queued, but processing is not yet complete.

questions.prompt: What header should be provided to implement optimistic concurrency control and avoid lost updates in REST APIs?
questions.explanation: If-Match with an entity tag (ETag) allows the server to verify the resource has not changed before applying updates (returning 412 if mismatched).

questions.prompt: What is the primary purpose of the `HttpOnly` flag on authentication session cookies?
options: Prevents client-side scripts from reading the cookie, mitigating Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) token theft
Encrypts the packet payload over HTTP without SSL
Ensures cookies expire after exactly 60 minutes
Allows cross-origin requests without CORS headers
questions.explanation: HttpOnly cookies cannot be accessed via document.cookie in JavaScript, protecting authentication tokens from malicious scripts.

questions.prompt: How does Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) differ from Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)?
options: CSRF tricks the user's browser into executing unwanted actions on an authenticated application; XSS injects malicious client-side code
CSRF only affects mobile applications while XSS affects web browsers
CSRF is mitigated purely by HTML sanitization
There is no difference; both are database injection techniques
questions.explanation: CSRF exploits ambient credentials (cookies) sent automatically by the browser, whereas XSS executes attacker JavaScript inside the victim's origin.

questions.prompt: In the Next.js App Router, what is the default rendering paradigm for components in the `app` directory?
questions.explanation: In Next.js App Router, all components inside the app directory are React Server Components by default unless explicitly marked with 'use client'.

questions.prompt: What utility class in Tailwind CSS flexbox layout centers items along the cross-axis?
questions.explanation: items-center maps to align-items: center in CSS.

questions.prompt: What is the key benefit of using a B-Tree index on a PostgreSQL column?
options: It provides O(log N) lookup, insertion, and range queries for equality and comparisons (<, <=, =, >=, >)
It compresses all text data by 90%
It enforces that the table can only contain numeric values
It replaces the need for foreign keys
questions.explanation: B-Tree indexes maintain a balanced tree suitable for equality and range query execution.

questions.prompt: When testing asynchronous React components with React Testing Library, which query method should you use to wait for an element that appears after an API call?
questions.explanation: findBy* returns a Promise that rejects on timeout or resolves when the element appears, wrapping waitFor internally.

codingTasks.prompt: Implement a `debounce(fn, delay)` higher-order function that delays invocation until after `delay` milliseconds have elapsed since the last time it was invoked. Include a `.cancel()` method on the returned function.

sqlTasks.prompt: Given a table `orders(id INTEGER, customer_id INTEGER, amount REAL, status TEXT, created_at TEXT)`, write a SELECT query that returns `customer_id` and total spent `total_spent` for all customers who have spent strictly more than 500 in 'completed' orders, ordered by `total_spent` DESC.
sqlTasks.starterCode:
-- Write your SQL query below
SELECT customer_id, SUM(amount) AS total_spent
FROM orders
...

visibleTests.input: SELECT count(*) FROM (SELECT customer_id FROM orders WHERE status='completed' GROUP BY customer_id HAVING SUM(amount) > 500);

hiddenTests.input: SELECT customer_id, round(SUM(amount), 2) as total_spent FROM orders WHERE status='completed' GROUP BY customer_id HAVING SUM(amount) > 500 ORDER BY total_spent DESC LIMIT 1;
SELECT count(*) FROM (SELECT customer_id FROM orders WHERE status='cancelled' GROUP BY customer_id HAVING SUM(amount) > 500);

sqlTasks.prompt: Given tables `users(id, name, created_at)` and `logins(id, user_id, login_time)`, write a query to list users who have logged in at least 3 times in the last 7 days.
sqlTasks.starterCode:
-- Write your SQL query below
SELECT u.id, u.name, COUNT(l.id) AS login_count
FROM users u
JOIN logins l ON u.id = l.user_id
...

hiddenTests.input: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT user_id FROM logins GROUP BY user_id HAVING count(*) >= 3);

projects.prompt:
Mini-Project: Design and implement a secure User Registration and JWT Auth endpoint in Node.js/Express. Requirements:
1. POST /api/register with email and password.
2. Validates email format and password minimum 8 characters.
3. Hashes password using bcrypt.
4. Rejects duplicate emails with HTTP 409 Conflict.
5. Returns HTTP 201 with `{ user: { id, email } }` and sets an HttpOnly cookie.

rubric.label: Endpoint Functionality
rubric.description: Registers users with correct HTTP status codes (201, 400, 409).

rubric.label: Password Hashing & Security
rubric.description: Bcrypt hashing with proper salt rounds; passwords never stored or returned in plain text.

rubric.label: Error Handling & Input Validation
rubric.description: Structured JSON error responses for malformed email, weak passwords, and database exceptions.

rubric.label: Session & Token Architecture
rubric.description: Clean JWT payload design with HttpOnly, SameSite, and Secure cookie flags.
